analysis_amendment.authorization: Build-time practical tolerance set to 10% before the first inferential look.
analysis_amendment.timing: Recorded after confirmatory collection started and before any confirmatory inferential look. Original 5% protocol is retained; this is an explicit post-start amendment, not the original preregistration.
analysis_amendment.selection_basis: Practical tolerance specified independently of confirmatory effect estimates and confidence intervals; first look selected from exact interval feasibility and paired collection waves.

unchanged.stop_rule: All72 treatment timing contrasts establish a nonzero median effect or equivalence within the registered margin; all12 A/A control intervals establish equivalence. Correctness/provenance gates must pass.

analysis_amendment.interpretation: 10% is the build practical-equivalence margin, not a claim of power or guaranteed precision at 14 observations. Retain runtime margin 3%, all platforms/levels/contrasts, alpha spending, all data and correctness/model-validity gates. If unresolved at 14, continue to 28, 56, and so on.

verified_facts: All 56 scheduled allocation reports at the frozen revision were independently verified; no confirmatory failure or excluded slow sample.
Fourteen distinct runner allocation identities per platform; seven successive waves with two concurrent allocations per platform.
Rust/Maturin versions, source fingerprints, Cargo settings, Python versions, resolver requirements and resolved outputs match within each platform.
All 84 simultaneous intervals resolve under the amended rules, including all twelve A/A controls.
Descriptive order and wave review retains the full observed variation; no additional hypothesis tests or timing-based exclusions.
Every published analysis field and measurement was compared to its retained raw report; all numerical inferential output reproduced exactly.
scope_and_limits: Population statements assume independent, representative allocations from the listed runner pools. Unique allocation names do not prove distinct physical hosts or absence of shared infrastructure/time dependence.
Linux x86-64 includes thirteen AMD EPYC allocations and one Intel Xeon allocation with different RAM capacity, all under the same requested label; results are for the sampled pool, not one vendor.
Native timings do not estimate production manylinux CI on a smaller runner.
Confidence intervals concern population median paired effects, not guaranteed limits for future individual builds.
